````text
# #4996: Patch: PIP's text says "performance improvement plan"
Opened by @MaxGoetzmann.

### What it does

Stinkyscape+ #94 **PIP** (`stinkyscapeplus-094`, SPEC §8.12) tells players a Unit is put on a "performance **enhancement** plan". A PIP is a performance **improvement** plan. Change the visible text on both faces to say "performance improvement plan", and add a ruling so every face, in every language the client shows, keeps that term word for word.

The Simplified Chinese faces already say 绩效改进计划 (performance improvement plan) in `crates/cards/card-text.yaml`, so they stay as they are. The new ruling's test locks them in.

**This is a change to the card's words only.** The rules stay the same: one target, the `kill_deadline` effect, `{count}`/`{count2}` turns, the Radiant face's `{the}` The Coins.

Where the old wording appears now (from `git grep -n "performance enhancement"` on main, f8c40d93):

| File | What to do |
|---|---|
| `spec/08-catalog/8.12-stinkyscape-plus.md` line 170, PIP's row | Change both faces. The spec is the only source of card text (`docs/ADDING_CARDS.md` §1, row 1). |
| `crates/cards/catalog.json` ~32631 (base) and ~32635 (radiant) | Change both `text`s: `Put a Unit on a performance improvement plan: it has …` |
| `crates/cards/src/scripts/stinkyscape_plus/c094_pip.rs` header (line 2) | Change the quoted base text. |
| `crates/engine/tests/rules/fixtures/combat_reactions.rs` line 51 | Change the doc comment that quotes PIP's shape. |
| `JackiOh_StinkyscapePlus_Cards.md` lines 1003 and 1005 (the designer's source note) | Change both lines so REVIEW Part A doesn't report a gap between the spec and the source. The owner made this call (this issue). |
| `crates/cards/patches/v*.json` (shipped history) | **Leave these alone.** Shipped patches and their snapshots are never reopened (`docs/ADDING_CARDS.md` §3). Replays fold under the version they were played on. |

**The patch.** A change to a card's words is a micro (`tier:micro`, `kind:cards`). Claim it with a pending fragment:

```
cargo jackioh patches "PIP says performance improvement plan" --source "#4996" --notes "Stinkyscape+ #94 PIP's text reads 'performance improvement plan' (was 'performance enhancement plan')."
```

Then write its `player` note by hand, one line under `text`, e.g. `PIP: now says "performance improvement plan".` (`docs/issues-and-patches.md`, Patch notes players read). The script only reads `count`, `count2` and `the`, not the card's words. So according to §3 of ADDING_CARDS it needs no `KEPT_SCRIPTS` entry. Before you push, run `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` to check this: it should find no card playing differently, so no `--plays`.

### The ruling

Add a new note, **R4996000** (`spec/rulings/R4996000.md`, the first number in this issue's block). Put its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/4996.md` (CLAUDE.md rule 3; `spec/README.md`, Adding a ruling). What it rules:

> **PIP names the plan word for word.** Every face of Stinkyscape+ #94 PIP (base and Radiant) contains the exact phrase "performance improvement plan" in English, and in every other language the client shows (`card-text.yaml`'s locales: Simplified Chinese, `zh`, today) that language's standard term for one. In Simplified Chinese that is 绩效改进计划. No face says it any other way, such as "performance enhancement plan", "performance plan" or "PEP". A language added later must name the plan by its own standard term, and this ruling's test covers it from the day it lands.

Proving test, named after the ruling (`fn r4996000_…`), e.g. in `crates/cards/tests/cross/chinese.rs` or PIP's own `mod tests`:
- both English faces of `stinkyscapeplus-094` in the catalog contain `performance improvement plan`, and neither contains `enhancement`;
- both `zh` faces (`crates/cards/chinese.json`, which `card-text.yaml` writes) contain `绩效改进计划`;
- it walks every locale the card text has, so a new language with no entry in the test's term table fails it, rather than skipping it.

### Acceptance

- [ ] `git grep -n "performance enhancement"` finds nothing outside `crates/cards/patches/v*.json` (the shipped history).
- [ ] The ruling note R4996000 and its `spec/pending/4996.md` paragraph exist, and `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.
- [ ] The proving test `r4996000_…` passes, and fails if the catalog's text goes back to "enhancement" or the `zh` face drops 绩效改进计划.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh catalog check`, `cargo jackioh patches check` and `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` pass.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-cards c094_pip` and `cargo test -p jackioh-cards --test cross` pass.

### Blocked by, part of

None.

1. `spec/08-catalog/8.12-stinkyscape-plus.md`, row 170. One edit whose find spans both face cells: find `performance enhancement plan, they have 1 turn to get a kill otherwise they are destroyed | Put a Unit on a performance enhancement plan` (matches once: the `|` is the cell boundary between the base and Radiant faces), replace with the same string with both occurrences as `performance improvement plan`. Then append the ruling link to the description cell: find `the 3 ↑ (the Radiant face's). Built by S18 (#3557). |`, replace with `the 3 ↑ (the Radiant face's). Built by S18 (#3557). 3. `crates/cards/src/scripts/stinkyscape_plus/c094_pip.rs`, line 2. Find `//!   Base:    "Put a Unit on a performance enhancement plan, they have {count} turn to get a kill` → `improvement` (matches once). Leave `pip()`, `script()`, `ID`, `mod tests` alone.

---
id: R4996000

A language added later must name the plan by its own standard term, and this ruling's test covers it from the day it lands. It edits [[§8.12]]'s S+ #94 row, the faces' words alone.

It edits [[§8.12]]'s S+ #94 row, the faces' words alone, and takes R4996000, the first number of issue #4996's block.`
9. Add the proving test at the end of `crates/tools/tests/export_card_text.rs` (it already imports `jackioh_cards::CATALOG` and reads `card-text.yaml` through `yaml_serde`; this file is chosen because it is the only test that sees every locale key — pure crates cannot parse YAML per rule 4, so `cross/chinese.rs` and the card's own `mod tests` can only see locales with compiled-in sidecars; precedent: R1303's `proven_in` already lists this file):
```rust
#[test]
fn r4996000_pip_names_the_plan_in_every_locale() {
    // R4996000: S+ #94 PIP names a performance improvement plan on every face,
    // in English and in every locale card-text.yaml shows (`zh` today).
    const ID: &str = "stinkyscapeplus-094";
    const TERMS: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
        ("en", "performance improvement plan"),
        ("zh", "绩效改进计划"),
    ];
    const NOT_WORDS: &[&str] = &["enhancement", "PEP", "performance plan"];
    const META: &[&str] = &["flavour", "artist", "voice"];
    let term = |locale: &str| {
        TERMS
            .iter()
            .find(|(code, _)| *code == locale)
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("R4996000: no term for locale {locale:?}: add its row to TERMS"))
            .1
    };
    let card = &CATALOG[ID];
    for face in [&card.base.text, &card.radiant.text] {
        assert!(face.contains(term("en")), "R4996000: {face:?} lacks the plan's name");
        for other in NOT_WORDS {
            assert!(!face.contains(other), "R4996000: {face:?} says it as {other:?}");
        }
    }
    let text = std::fs::read_to_string(YAML).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{YAML}: {error}"));
    let root: yaml_serde::Mapping =
        yaml_serde::from_str(&text).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("card-text.yaml: {error}"));
    let entry = root
        .get(&yaml_serde::Value::String(ID.to_string()))
        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("card-text.yaml: no {ID} entry"));
    let entry = entry.as_mapping().unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("card-text.yaml: {ID} is not a mapping"));
    let mut seen: Vec<&str> = vec!["en"];
    for (key, value) in entry {
        let Some(field) = key.as_str() else { continue };
        if META.contains(&field) {
            continue;
        }
        let faces = value
            .as_mapping()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("card-text.yaml: {ID}.{field} is not a locale"));
        let get = |face: &str| {
            faces
                .get(&yaml_serde::Value::String(face.to_string()))
                .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
                .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("card-text.yaml: {ID}.{field} has no {face}"))
        };
        for face in [get("base"), get("radiant")] {
            assert!(face.contains(term(field)), "R4996000: {ID}.{field} lacks its term");
        }
        seen.push(field);
    }
    let mut want: Vec<&str> = TERMS.iter().map(|(code, _)| *code).collect();
    seen.sort_unstable();
    want.sort_unstable();
    assert_eq!(seen, want, "R4996000: locales shown and locales in TERMS differ");
}
```
A locale added to `card-text.yaml` later reaches the loop as a non-`META` mapping and fails on the missing `TERMS` row instead of passing silently; a removed locale fails the final equality.
10. Prove the test locks the wording (temporary flips, each restored immediately, running only the new test between): `sed -i 's/performance improvement plan: it has/performance enhancement plan: it has/' crates/cards/catalog.json`, then `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test export_card_text r4996000` must FAIL; restore with `sed -i 's/performance enhancement plan: it has/performance improvement plan: it has/' crates/cards/catalog.json`, test must PASS. Then `sed -i 's/绩效改进计划/绩效增强计划/' crates/cards/card-text.yaml` (confirm beforehand it hits exactly the 2 PIP lines), test must FAIL; restore with the reverse `sed`, test must PASS. If any restore leaves the tree wrong, the greps and suite in step 11 catch it.

## Done when

- [ ] Both PIP faces read "performance improvement plan" in the §8.12 row, `catalog.json`, the script header, the fixture comment and the designer source; `git grep -n "performance enhancement"` finds nothing outside `crates/cards/patches/v*.json`.

- `classify` unexpectedly naming playing cards: the script and params are untouched, so this should not happen; if it does, stop and report rather than adding `--plays` blindly.
````
